title: For Loop Patterns
story: You're hosting a party and need to greet every guest as they arrive: "Welcome, Mia!" "Welcome, Jay!" "Welcome, Priya!" Instead of writing the same line over and over, you can put all the names in a list and let a `for` loop handle the greetings automatically!
why: For loops are the cleanest way to process lists of things — from names in a contact list to items in a shopping cart to days in a month.
analogy: A for loop is like a conveyor belt — items come to you one at a time, and you process each the same way.
expected_output:
Today is Mon
Today is Tue
Today is Wed
Today is Thu
Today is Fri
try_it: Create a list of your 5 favorite foods. Use a for loop to print "Yum! I love [food]" for each one. Then try a list of numbers and compute something inside the loop!
tips: The loop variable name is up to you — `for item in list` or `for x in numbers` both work fine
The list can contain anything: strings, numbers, even other lists!
Inside the loop body, you can use the loop variable in calculations, comparisons, or string building
common_mistakes: Forgetting that `for` iterates through the whole list automatically — you don't need a counter or to check the length
Naming the loop variable the same as a variable outside the loop — this can cause confusing bugs!
